title: Shafali Verma Rewrites Record Books as India Crush Pakistan in Women's Asia Cup
excerpt: The 22-year-old opener becomes the youngest and fastest player to reach 3,000 Women's T20I runs during India's seven-wicket demolition of Pakistan in Dubai.
body:
• Shafali Verma became the youngest player (22 years, 220 days) and fastest by balls faced (2,182 deliveries) to reach 3,000 runs in Women's T20 Internationals.
  • She overtook Ireland's Gaby Lewis for the age record and Australia's Alyssa Healy for the balls-faced record during India's Asia Cup clash against Pakistan.
  • India bowled Pakistan out for 55 — Pakistan's lowest-ever T20I score — and chased the target in 8.4 overs for a seven-wicket win.
  • India completed a perfect group stage with three wins from three matches in the Women's Asia Cup 2026.

A Milestone in Six Balls

Shafali Verma needed just seven runs heading into India's Women's Asia Cup 2026 Group A match against Pakistan at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday. She collected them with her trademark aggression, scoring a quickfire 12 off six balls — opening with a six off the very first delivery from Sadia Iqbal — before being dismissed by Pakistan captain Fatima Sana, according to NDTV Sports.

https://x.com/SonySportsNetwk/status/2096276080349057405

At 22 years and 220 days, Verma became the youngest cricketer in the world to reach 3,000 runs in Women's T20 Internationals, overtaking Ireland's Gaby Lewis, who held the previous record at 24 years and 347 days. She also became the fastest to the milestone by balls faced, reaching it in 2,182 deliveries compared to Australia's Alyssa Healy, who held the previous mark at 2,321 balls before retiring earlier this year, according to CREX.

Multiple Records in One Innings

The six off the first ball of the innings added yet another record. Verma became the only player in Women's T20I history to hit a six off the opening delivery of an innings on multiple occasions — she had previously done so against Pakistan at the T20 World Cup 2026 in Birmingham, according to NDTV Sports.

Verma is now the 16th woman overall and the third Indian — after Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur — to join the 3,000-run club in Women's T20Is. Her career numbers through 114 T20Is read 3,005 runs at an average of 28.08, with 19 scores of fifty or more.

India's Bowlers Dismantle Pakistan

The records came in the context of a comprehensive demolition. India's bowlers skittled Pakistan for just 55 — a new record-low T20I score for Pakistan, coming in their 200th match in the format. Shree Charani and Prema Rawat claimed three wickets each, while Deepti Sharma picked up two as Pakistan's batting collapsed from a promising 27 without loss after four overs, according to LatestLY.

Verma herself contributed with the ball, taking 1 for 10 in three overs, including the key wicket of opener Muneeba Ali. The dismissal sparked a fiery send-off from Verma, which Pakistan captain Fatima Sana later reciprocated after taking the Indian opener's wicket during the chase, according to CREX.

"I still believe Pakistan is the best side in this Asia Cup to lift the trophy because the conditions really suit us."

— Wahab Riaz, Pakistan team mentor, after the defeat

India's Perfect Group Stage

India chased down the target of 56 in just 8.4 overs, with captain Harmanpreet Kaur finishing unbeaten on 18 and Deepti Sharma contributing 12 not out. The win completed a flawless group-stage campaign: three matches, three victories against Thailand, Hong Kong, and Pakistan, collecting all six available points.

Pakistan face a do-or-die encounter against Hong Kong in their final group match, needing a win to secure a place in the last four.

What's Next

Verma's blistering form ahead of the knockout stages is a significant boost for India's title defence in the Asia Cup and their upcoming campaign at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, where the women's cricket tournament begins September 17. At just 22, she has already rewritten the record books and shows no signs of slowing down.
